title: Clock-Test Transition
statement: Let $M$ be a finite-state Boolean Turing machine, let $x,y$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Choose a Boolean tag $b$, a family of natural-number movement counts $n$, a record word, and natural numbers $T,t$ with $t<T$. One step of the recorder machine from the clock-test phase of the corresponding recorder configuration advances the clock head from position $t$ to $t+1$ and enters the source-release phase, leaving the other configuration data unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: A finite-state Boolean Turing machine M
A source configuration c on input y
Natural numbers T and t with t < T
replaced: For every source configuration, tag, movement counts, record, clock budget $T$, and logical time $t < T$, one recorder step from the clock-test phase reads the live unary clock cell, advances only the clock head from $t$ to $t+1$, and enters the source-release phase; no source head moves and no record bit is appended.
